newsitem.title: FRANCE: France 3 sees cost from M6 competition.
newsitem.headline: France 3 sees cost from M6 competition.

text.p: If private French terrestrial TV channel M6-Metropole TV were allowed to broadcast regional programmes, this would cost public channel France 3 some 300 million francs a year, Xavier Gouyou-Beauchamps, chairman of France Television, told a Parliamentary committee on Wednesday.
"There is a risk of losing at least 300 million francs in receipts a year," he said.
France 3 currently specialises in regional programming.
"The conditions of competition with M6 are not clear. M6 has a more favourable regime than all other operators for quotas," Gouyou-Beauchamps said.
French television channels by law have to carry a fixed percentage, or quota, of French-made programmes.

Parliament is currently examining a broadcasting bill due to be finalised by the summer. Recently the Senate upper house rejected an ammendment allowing M6 to broadcast regional programmes, but the proposal is due to be re-examined by the lower house National Assembly this month.
